summary: Cush names a son of Ham, the land associated with his descendants, and people from that land. Psalm 7 also names a man of Benjamin called Cush. The heading identifies his tribe but gives no genealogy.

senses.definition: A land and its people. Tirhakah is called king of Cush. Isaiah names Cush beside Egypt when describing peoples taken into captivity.
Ebed-melech is identified as a Cushite serving at the king’s house. The feminine form describes the woman Moses married.

evidence.locator: ISA 20:4 word 10, translating the people of Cush

senses.definition: Habakkuk sees Cushan’s tents in distress and the curtains of Midian trembling. The parallel places two tent-dwelling peoples beside one another.

words.summary: The connection of Cushan with Cush remains uncertain.

senses.definition: The Ethiopian travelling home from worship in Jerusalem serves the queen of Cush.
In the Peshitta the royal title identifies the people over whom the queen rules.

cognates.note: The Egyptian place name corresponds to biblical Cush in the Nile region. The route by which the name entered Hebrew is uncertain.

note: The personal-name file owns the two Cush indexes, which share surface forms with the land. The name Cushan-rishathaim is already in names/cushan-rishathaim.json. Cuthah (2 Kings 17:24) is a separate place. SEDRA lexemes 1500 and 1501 occur together in Acts 8:27.
